_comment: Two flat panels, not two boxes.
The map used to be a one-pixel-thick cube, which meant its four narrow
sides had to be given a UV of their own. There is nothing on a torn
parchment texture that reads as the *edge* of a sheet, so whatever slice
they were given looked like a mistake from every angle but head-on.
A cube with a zero-length axis renders as a single quad instead: the map
is a sheet with no thickness, drawn from both sides, and there are no side
faces left to mis-texture. Each panel is 15 pixels rather than 16, so it
sits a hair inside the block it occupies and reads as an object placed on
a surface rather than as the surface itself, and each is offset a fraction
off that surface so the two planes cannot z-fight.
